item.title: Juno Artist Spotlight – William Prince
item.description: From deep family roots to big, soul-searching ideas, William Prince’s Further From the Country is more than just an album—it’s a statement. Dive into the story behind the music and the artist shaping it. For the full article profile on Contemporary Roots Album of the Year “2026” nominee William Prince, check out https://junoawards.ca/nomination/2026-contemporary-roots-album-of-the-year-i-william-prince/

item.title: Juno Artist Spotlight – Crystal Shawanda
item.description: From country stardom at 19 to becoming a powerhouse in the blues world, Crystal Shawanda’s journey is anything but ordinary. Discover how she carved her own path and made history along the way. Blues Album of the Year “Sing Pretty Blues” Nominee Crystal Shawanda’s full story is here: https://junoawards.ca/nomination/2026-blues-album-of-the-year-i-crystal-shawanda/

item.title: Juno Artist Spotlight – Morgan Toney
item.description: Blending Mi’kmaq tradition with Celtic roots, Morgan Toney is creating something entirely new. His album Heal the Divide is a powerful mix of culture, language, and connection—honouring the past while looking ahead. For the full story about Traditional Roots Album of the Year “Heal The Divide” Nominee Morgan Toney, check it out here: https://junoawards.ca/nomination/2026-traditional-roots-album-of-the-year-i-morgan-toney/

item.title: Juno Artist Spotlight – PIQSIQ
item.description: Inspired by the stark beauty of the North, Inuit throat singers Inuksuk Mackay and Tiffany Ayalik create powerful, ever-evolving soundscapes. Their latest album Legends blends ancient tradition with modern innovation—no two performances the same. “Legends” was nominated for Global Music Album of the Year

item.title: Juno Artist Spotlight – Sherryl Sewepagaham
item.description: From Cree-Dene roots to national stages, Sherryl Sewepagaham brings culture, education, and music together in powerful ways. In collaboration with the Canadian Chamber Choir, her work helps shape a vibrant, shared Canadian sound. For the full story about the Classical Album of the Year (Large Ensemble) “Where Waters Meet” Nominee, check out: https://junoawards.ca/nomination/2026-classical-album-of-the-year-large-ensemble-i-canadian-chamber-choir-featuring-sherryl-sewepagaham/

item.title: Juno Artist Spotlight – Aysanabee
item.description: From a remote Northwestern Ontario community to major stages across the world, Aysanabee is redefining indie music. His new album Edge of the Earth dives into identity, sacrifice, and self-discovery—marking a bold new chapter. Aysanabee is nominated for Alternative Album of the Year “Edge Of The Earth” The full story is here: https://junoawards.ca/nomination/2026-alternative-album-of-the-year-i-aysanabee/

item.title: Juno Artist Spotlight – SonReal and Snotty Nose Rez Kids
item.description: From chart-topping hits to fearless storytelling, Canadian artists SonReal and Snotty Nose Rez Kids are making waves. SonReal’s music has racked up hundreds of millions of streams, while SNRK use hip-hop to challenge, celebrate, and amplify Indigenous voices. Two different sounds, one undeniable impact. For the complete story about how Rap Single of the Year “DUMB” came to be, check out the full story: https://junoawards.ca/nomination/2026-rap-single-of-the-year-i-sonreal-snotty-nose-rez-kids/
